data.claim: Today only CLI and stdio MCP with a bind-mounted repo work. No HTTP transport or ddflow serve exists; no-fs, remote and devcontainer are planned (P-remote NS-*, ST-*, DCF-*), not built. lean tools/list = 16 tools 32 KB; no annotations; next_hints default off; ddflow_view board returns 1.5 MB unbounded.
data.falsifier: ddflow serve or a non-stdio transport exists on main, or a fs-less run of claim/gate/merge passes in tests
data.mechanism: Server reads .ddflow/events/*.jsonl, rules, config and runs git worktree, command gates and reviewers locally (infra/worktree.py:248, services/gates/runner.py:209, api/lifecycle/merge.py:51). Storage seam ST-* and run-yourself envelope NS-run-yourself are open.
data.probe: in-process mcp.Server tools/list per DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS profile and tools/call sizes; ddflow serve -> invalid choice
data.probe_output: lean 16/32284 B, core 34/38955, standard 81/76866, families 24/54332, hot+families 36/72302, all 124/112348; instructions 1.7-2.5K chars; brief 4018 B; status 19767 B; list task 10568 B; board 1507998 B; zero annotations/outputSchema
data.question: Does every ddflow feature work via CLI, MCP (smallest surface), and with/without local fs (docker, remote, devcontainer), for external front ends too?

data.claim: ddflow's self-observation is strong on derived workflow statistics (ddflow metrics) and weak on correlation ids, app logs, cost and alert consumption; observing managed projects' observability needs only extensions of P-lifecycle LF-feedback, SC-probe, IA-release, TM-metrics plus 3 small tasks, no new phase.
data.falsifier: If a run/trace id can be derived from existing fields (agent+subject+lamport) for every tool call, correlation-id task is unneeded; if PM-agent-calls already covers the MCP request log, the request-log task duplicates it.
data.mechanism: Event log (132468 events, 117 MB, 834 shards, 9021 subjects) already is the audit/telemetry source; metrics fold derives p50/p90 from it; gaps measured below. Managed-project work reuses stack profile, proposal, gate and feedback-loop records.
data.probe: python scan of .ddflow/events/*.jsonl; ddflow metrics; ddflow health; ddflow cadence; grep logging in ddflow/
data.probe_output: events carry only agent,data,id,kind,lamport,schema,subject,ts (no run/trace/tool-call id); 0 uses of python logging; resource evidence (maxrss_kb) on 44 of 22231 gate outcome events (0.2%); lease.renewed = 29.8% of events but 8.5% of bytes; cadence health_watch overdue 632225 s (target 900), integration_tests due 1485 tasks (every 5); gate outcomes ci fail 38%, critic 55%, rubber_duck 57%; cycle p50 1.3h p90 8.5h; queue wait p90 36.1h; no token/cost field on any gate/review event (matches of _tokens are prompt text).
data.question: What observability does ddflow have of itself, what is missing, and how should ddflow monitor observability work in the projects it manages; which ideas of the Railway observability primer apply?

data.budget: about 90 min, read-only, no installs; orjson speedup not measured (THEORETICAL)
data.claim: Every read verb pays O(total log): parse+merge+fold = about 4.4 s cold at 132k (33 us/event; 15-30 s and 2.2 GB RSS at 1M synthetic), repeated 2-5 times per command, plus a restamp that fires whenever ANY agent appended. A State checkpoint plus tail fold, single load per command, no restamp on foreign appends, lazy numpy import and one-pass doctor remove about 85-95 percent without touching the log or adding a database.
data.falsifier: Prototype State-pickle checkpoint plus tail fold: if show on the real log is not under 1.5 s idle with State byte-identical to a full fold, or if a second process appending in a loop does not stop read verbs from calling batch.apply after the restamp fix, the claim is false.
data.mechanism: The log is append-only per agent shard and fold is pure and deterministic, so State at a verified shard-prefix mark plus the appended tail equals a full fold unless a merged clone brings an event sorting before the mark (detected, falls back to an older rung). Waste is elsewhere: keep_stamped compares the global log.mark so a busy log restamps after read verbs; _load_fresh runs 2-5 times; embed.py imports numpy at startup; doctor re-scans 1.3 GB of transcripts per consumed ask; the marshal read snapshot costs more than json parsing.
data.probe: cProfile and wall timers per phase (scratch/phases.py), py-spy 150 s on doctor, python -X importtime, DDFLOW_SNAPSHOT=0/1 A/B, DDFLOW_WAVES_AUTO_STAMP=false A/B on show, logfixture.generate at 250k/500k/1M, State pickle dump/load, git/count scans of the event log; load average 13-66 on 192 cores, each timing repeated 2-3 times
data.probe_output: version 0.99 s wall but user 8.2 s (user 0.86 with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; numpy via ddflow.services.embed). Cold _load_fresh phases: read_all 3.4 s, fold 0.9 s, warm read_all 0.8 s. Command wall at 132k: next 6-11, show 6-18 (bimodal: restamp 4-16 s when another agent appended), board 9-18, recall 15.5, status 22.5 (622 git subprocesses 9.8 s), brief 40-43, doctor ~870 s (76 percent in harness.verify rescanning 1264 transcripts, 228 consumed asks). show with auto_stamp off: 22.8 s to 8.0 s under cProfile. Snapshot ON 3.6 s vs OFF 2.8 s cold at 132k; 27 vs 15 s at 1M. Synthetic cold load 32k 0.8 s, 66k 1.5-2.1 s, 132k 2.8 s, 250k 3.3 s, 500k 7-8 s (1.1 GB), 1M 15-30 s (2.2 GB). State pickle 85 MB (items 74 MB), load 0.47 s vs fold 0.9 s. index.db: 46 fingerprint files, 5.0 GB. In-process parse cache holds 100000 of 132555 events (max_cached_events ceiling already crossed). Event mix: lease.renewed 29.8 percent, gate.passed+failed 53 percent of bytes.
data.question: Where does ddflow time go on the 132k-event, 116 MB, 834-shard log, how does it scale to 1M and 10M events, and which upgrade-safe, derived-data-only changes fix it?

data.claim: Tiny fixes (src+other <=10 changed lines, <=6 files, no hot engine path) are ~11% of completed items (169 of 1510, 2026-09-28..11-03) but only ~5% of gate-hours (70 of 1415 h); skipping their reviews would miss a confirmed MEDIUM+ finding in ~12-20% of them, so the safe win is bundling the shared gates (ci/unit_tests/standards) plus ONE combined review per bundle, not review skipping; a text predictor is no better than base rate, so a post-hoc diff guard must decide.
data.falsifier: A replay of the 169 tiny-cold fixes through a bundler (N<=10, path-disjoint) that shows <20% gate wall-time saved, or >1 culprit-attributed red bundle in 10, or a post-hoc guard that demotes >40% of bundled items.
data.mechanism: Per-item fixed gate cost (ci 475 s, unit_tests 560 s, rubber_duck 272 s, critic 195 s median for tiny) dominates a 10-line change; same-day tiny pairs overlap on paths in only 12 of 535 pairs, so path-disjoint bundles of 4-6 are common. Existing: doc_pipeline by actual diff (services/docsonly.py), [chore], [review].combined_under_lines, P-batch-gates (D-BG-Q4: reviewer never skipped), TA-fastlane (queue cap only).
data.probe: python over .ddflow/events (133458 events): item gates/triage/bug events joined to git diff --numstat landed_before..landed_after excluding .ddflow and docs/ddflow
data.probe_output: fix tasks 631/1510; tiny-cold fixes 169; findings confirmed MEDIUM+ tiny 30/149 (src>0 only 7/37); gate-hours tiny 70/1415; median lead 37 vs 87 min; text predictor precision 0.17-0.24 vs base 0.15
data.question: Can tiny, safe fixes be bundled or gate-lightened on a fast track, and what does the real log say about how many, how costly and how safe?
